rules: This baseline may only SHRINK. CI rejects any commit that adds an entry.
A new unprotected mutating action fails the build - it is not silently appended.
A protected or removed action must disappear from this file.
Renaming a controller or action does NOT create a new allowance: the id changes, so the old id becomes stale (diagnostic CBA007) and the new id is unlisted (CBA001 error).
No blanket suppression. No project-wide disable switch.

The 'gaps' figure and the entries list are the ENFORCED invariant and may only shrink. The mutating, attributeProtected and inBodyProtected figures are descriptive totals of the tree and legitimately grow when protected endpoints are added; frozenBaselineHistory records every such change with its reason.

frozenBaselineHistory.note: Report Studio V1 added ONE controller, ReportStudioApiController, with FIVE endpoints - Fields, Validate, Preview, Save and Export. Growth is +5 mutating and +5 in-body protected, +0 attribute-protected and +0 debt, and the arithmetic still closes: 157 + 115 + 143 = 415. Every one of the five authorizes in-body through IReportAuthorizationService.AuthorizeReportAsync at the boundary before it acts, resolving the dataset's report definition from the caller's own permitted list. CBA001 FIRED ON ALL FOUR POSTS when the controller first landed and was fixed by ADDING THAT GATE - not by a baseline entry, not by a suppression, and not by reshaping a write as a GET. NO entry was added, removed or edited; the gap figure stays 143 and the entries list is byte-identical; no CBA diagnostic was suppressed and the shrink-only rule was not relaxed. Only the descriptive totals moved, because production code was added - the case this file's own rules paragraph describes.
The accepted Stage 1 measurement. Reproduced exactly by the Roslyn analyzer with 0 classification disagreements across all 388 endpoints.

Batch A added three mutating endpoints - PlatformGrantsApiController.Create, .Revoke and .UpdateValidity - and one controller. All three are authorized in-body through IPlatformGrantWriter, which resolves the actor's administration tier and privilege ceiling via the real module access services. DEBT IS UNCHANGED AT 143 and no entry was added, removed or edited: the gap set still matches this file id for id. Only the descriptive totals moved, because production code was added.

Reconciles the descriptive totals with the modernization work that had accumulated in the working tree unrecorded. Growth is +19 mutating and +19 in-body protected, +0 attribute-protected and +0 debt - the signature of protected endpoints being added, and the arithmetic still closes: 157 + 110 + 143 = 410. COMPOSITION OF THE +19, every one authorized in-body through a real access service on the analyzer's approved authority list: (a) SEVEN Reporting write endpoints on ReportsCenterWriteApiController - SaveLayout, Fork, SetDefault, DeleteLayout, AddFavorite, RemoveFavorite, ReorderFavorites - each through IReportAuthorizationService.AuthorizeReportAsync or .AuthorizeTemplateAsync; (b) ELEVEN Tasks endpoints on TasksController - the Task Ecosystem checklist (Add/Remove/Reorder/Toggle), dependencies (Add/Remove), templates (Apply/Save/SetActive), BoardMove and TaskCommentAdd - each through ITasksAccessService.CanAsync; (c) ONE Calendar endpoint, CalendarController.SaveSchedule, through ICalendarAccessService.CanEventAsync. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not merely asserted: the gap set was rebuilt from the analyzer's own evidence file (docs/architecture/evidence/Roslyn-Authorization-Inventory.csv, written by the same run) and differenced against this file's entries - 143 vs 143, with ZERO ids present in the analyzer and absent here (which would be new debt) and ZERO present here and absent in the analyzer (which would be a stale entry). CalendarController.Save and .Delete are unauthorized but are NOT new debt: both were already frozen entries in this file, so Calendar arrived carrying pre-existing debt rather than adding to it. NO entry was added, removed or edited; the gap figure stays 143; no CBA diagnostic was suppressed and no baseline shrink-only rule was relaxed.

frozenBaselineHistory.stage: UAT dataset harness controller-count reconciliation (UAT dataset owner, 2026-08-12)
frozenBaselineHistory.note: Controller-count-only reconciliation for UatSeedController, the [DevOnly] UAT dataset harness on api/uat introduced by the UAT dataset owner. The analyzer's frozen CONTROLLER count moves 44 -> 45; NONE of the four figures that matter moves. Mutating stays 410, attribute-protected 157, in-body-protected 110 and debt 143, and 157 + 110 + 143 = 410 still closes. THE REASON IS MECHANICAL, not a judgement: every action on that controller is [HttpGet] - preflight, prime, seed, counts, cleanup - so the analyzer models the controller but finds no mutating endpoint on it to classify. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY rather than asserted: the analyzer's own evidence file docs/architecture/evidence/Roslyn-Authorization-Inventory.csv holds 410 rows and ZERO of them name UatSeed, which is the same 410 the frozen mutating total asserts, so the new controller contributed nothing to any protected category and nothing to the debt. NO entry in this file was added, removed or edited; count stays 143 and entries stays 143. No CBA diagnostic was suppressed, CBA001 was not weakened, no security attribute was removed, and no product authorization was changed to satisfy a count. The controller is not an unmeasured hole: it returns 404 outside Development via [CrossBuy.Models.DevOnly], is shared-key gated, and its own preflight refuses to write unless the live connection resolves to CrossBuyDev. Also recorded here: the passwordless GET api/uat/signin that briefly existed on this controller has been REMOVED in the same increment; UAT runtime automation now authenticates through the ordinary AccountController.Login / PasswordSignInAsync path.
